stories.title: Hundreds of tourists missing in Nepal: Travel advice and emergency contacts
stories.summary: European governments have issued safety guidance and emergency contacts for travellers as flooding and landslides disrupt transport across parts of Nepal. Hundreds of foreign tourists are reported missing after devastating flooding in Nepal struck an area popular with international travellers. The Nepal Tourism Board said on Thursday that 644 tourists were out of contact, including 517 foreign nationals. They include visitors from 19 European countries as well as China, the United States and Australia. It is urging travellers to inform the nearest police or security authority, local administration, travel agency, guide or tour operator of their location and in a statement said "please remain clam, stay informed and follow official safety instructions". The disaster has particularly affected Rasuwa and neighbouring Nuwakot, north of Kathmandu and close to Nepal's border with Tibet. The country is home to eight of the world's 10 highest mountains, including Mount Everest, and official figures show 1.16 million international tourists visited Nepal in 2025, including more than 165,000 who went trekking. What should travellers in Nepal do? European governments and other foreign embassies are advising travellers to follow instructions from Nepalese authorities and closely monitor local conditions. The embassies of Finland, France and the UK, together with Australia, Norway and Switzerland and the EU Delegation in Nepal, issued a joint statement urging people in affected areas to "follow the guidance of local authorities and official safety advisories as the situation continues to evolve". France warns that due to flooding and landslides telephone networks and internet connections can be cut for several days. Travellers are advised to check with local authorities before making journeys and to follow their instructions.

stories.title: NFL champions Seattle Seahawks sold to Khosla Group for record $9.6 billion
stories.summary: The price tag is an NFL record for a franchise sale and the second-highest valuation in North American sports history. The owners of the National Football League (NFL) in the United States have unanimously approved the sale of the Seattle Seahawks for a league-record price of $9.6bn to a group led by the Khosla family. The sales agreement was announced on July 11 and awaited approval at a special meeting of the owners in Atlanta on Wednesday to become official. The sale was in accordance with the wishes of the late team owner, Paul Allen. At least 24 of 32 owners were required to approve the sale, which was expected after the NFL’s finance and ownership policy committees voted unanimously last week to recommend ratification. “How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl?” said the multi-billionaire businessman Vinod Khosla, standing with his coowners, wife Neeru and son Neal. “We are incredibly lucky and humbled by this gift, I would say, from the Allen trust.” The estate of Paul G. Allen, which inherited the NFL team after his death in 2018, agreed to terms with the Khosla family after a search for a new owner. Allen’s will stipulated that the team be sold and assets be distributed to various charities. The price tag is an NFL record for a franchise sale. It is the second-highest valuation in North American sports history; the Los Angeles Lakers sold for $10 billion last year and were more recently valued at $12.5 billion, as Bob Iger and Josh Kushner plan to purchase a majority stake in the NBA team from Mark Walter.

stories.summary: The operator of the Hong Kong government’s 1823 platform will expand the use of artificial intelligence (AI) within this year to transcribe, summarise and triage residents’ inquiries, freeing frontline staff to handle more complicated cases. stories.title: Poland asks EU to fine Meta €250 million, urges action against scams and false ads
stories.summary: WARSAW, Aug 27 - Poland's Minister of Digital Affairs said on Wednesday he had asked the European Commission to impose a €250 million ($291.30 million) fine on Meta, accusing the social media company of failing to adequately tackle fraudulent advertisements..
article_sentences: "I also call on Meta to immediately introduce effective tools to eliminate scams, false advertising, and the promotion of illegal applications."
Meta has not immediately responded to a Reuters request for comment.
Meta Platform came under fire for allegations that its products were harmful to children and that the company was misleading the public about their safety.

stories.title: (LEAD) Lee orders mobilization of all resources to rescue S. Koreans affected by Nepal flooding
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 27 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday ordered the mobil...
article_sentences: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday ordered the mobilization of all available resources to rescue South Koreans affected by massive flooding in Nepal, as nine South Korean nationals there remain missing.
Lee issued the order during an emergency meeting, a day after catastrophic floods struck China and Nepal, with over 160 people confirmed dead so far and hundreds still missing.
As of Thursday, nine South Koreans -- all workers engaged in the construction of a hydroelectric power plant in Nepal -- remained unaccounted for, while 10 others were stranded.
The government dispatched an emergency response team to Nepal earlier in the day to aid in the search for the nationals.
"I ask you to do your utmost to safeguard the people's lives and safety by mobilizing all available resources, with the determination that nothing is too much," Lee told the meeting.
The president, in particular, stressed that overseas embassies and the dispatched response team, as well as other manpower and resources, should be fully mobilized for the rescue effort.
Lee also instructed officials to check whether any other nationals have been affected and ensure the safety of South Koreans in the affected areas to prevent further casualties.
"As this is an emergency situation, utmost efforts (should be made) to rescue those who can be rescued and search for (those who remain missing)," the president said.

The president stressed the importance of cooperating with the Nepalese government, instructing officials to activate all diplomatic channels to facilitate the deployment of resources needed to rescue South Korean nationals.

Lee also offered condolences to the Nepalese government and people over the catastrophe, instructing officials to review South Korea's assistance to Nepal in dealing with the disaster and rebuilding the country, including humanitarian assistance.

stories.title: Jeju police chief apologises over mishandled missing person cases
stories.summary: He also pledged a thorough and transparent investigation into the cases.
article_sentences: Jeju Police Commissioner Ko Pyeong-gi apologised after two missing person cases were wrongly closed and the individuals were later found dead.
A police officer falsely claimed to have contacted the missing people to close their cases, causing distress to the families.
Jeju police will conduct a full investigation and review all missing person cases to uncover any other errors or misconduct.
Jeju Police Commissioner Ko Pyeong-gi on Aug 27 issued a public apology after two people whose missing person cases were closed by a police officer on allegedly false grounds were later found dead.

“I bow my head in apology to the two deceased people who never made it back to their families, and to the bereaved families suffering grief beyond description,” Ko said in a statement at the Jeju Provincial.
Police Agency.

A Jeju police officer surnamed Bu is accused of closing the case of Jang Mi-ran, a 37-year-old woman who disappeared in May and was found dead on Aug 24, by falsely claiming that he had spoken to her.
Bu is accused of using the same method to close another case involving a man in his 60s, whose body was found on Aug 22.

“A police officer has a responsibility to protect the safety and lives of the people, yet he disregarded that duty and lied, leaving permanent scars on the families,” Ko said, also apologising to Jeju residents.
Ko pledged a thorough and transparent investigation into the cases.

stories.title: Russian forces continue their offensive unabated, chief of General Staff says
stories.summary: General Valery Gerasimov said the offensive continues in all directions
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 27.
Russian forces have been on the offensive across all directions of the special military operation, Chief of Russia’s General Staff Army General Valery Gerasimov said.
"Battlegroups have continued to accomplish tasks of the special military operation.
The offensive continues unabated in all directions," Gerasimov said as he inspected the Battlegroup South.
